q: How do I calculate emissions from trucks idling?
title: Truck idling emissions per hour
short: Multiply idling litres per hour by 2.68 kg CO2 per litre of diesel. Take the idle fuel rate from telematics or the engine data, not a guess, then multiply by idle hours from the tracker. Idling is already inside your fuel invoices, so report it as a sub-figure.

ul: Telematics or engine data that logs fuel while stationary.
A test: run the engine at idle for an hour and measure the tank drop.
Use an assumed rate only if labelled as one.

p: Idle fuel is part of the litres you already buy. Use the idling figure to target savings, not to add to the total.
Engine-off rules at loading bays, auto shut-off and cab heaters or coolers that do not need the engine all reduce idle hours.

example.title: Worked example: 20-truck fleet (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Idling at an assumed 2 litres per hour: 2 x 2.68 = 5.36 kg CO2 per hour
Fleet idling: 20 trucks x 2 hours a day x 25 days = 1,000 hours
example.note: The 2 litres per hour idle rate is an assumed input; replace it with your telematics figure.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.
